headline: FCA moves Consumer Duty into active enforcement, floats carve-out for overseas clients
summary: The UK's Financial Conduct Authority is shifting Consumer Duty from implementation to active supervision of brokers in 2026, tightening scrutiny of claims handling and pricing, while separately proposing to ease the Duty's application to business written for non-UK customers.

headline: Reliance Global Group recruits Coinbase and Capital One veteran as CTO
summary: Reliance Global Group named a new Chief Technology Officer with backgrounds from Coinbase and Capital One, alongside a new COO and EVP, to steer the company's AI-driven insurance product roadmap and its strategy of rolling up independent agencies.

headline: Duck Creek buys London underwriting-AI firm Send to link core systems with intelligent risk decisioning
summary: Core P&C software provider Duck Creek Technologies acquired London-based Send Technology Solutions, an AI-native underwriting engine that supports more than $26 billion in premium for commercial, specialty and MGA business.

headline: Turtlemint becomes India's second insurtech to go public
summary: Insurance distribution platform Turtlemint listed on the NSE and BSE after an IPO that raised roughly $106 million, marking only the second Indian insurtech to reach public markets and signaling growing investor confidence in the country's digital insurance distribution model.

headline: EU widens AI Act's high-risk net to cover more insurance underwriting
summary: New draft guidance on the EU AI Act's Annex III, issued in May 2026, extended high-risk classification to more insurance underwriting use cases, including long-term care, personal pensions and public health cover, ahead of obligations for high-risk insurance AI systems taking effect in August 2026.

headline: NAIC's multi-state AI oversight pilot heads toward a July checkpoint
summary: U.S. state regulators are running a 12-state pilot of the NAIC's new AI Systems Evaluation Tool through September 2026 to examine insurer AI governance, with a public working-group session planned for late July to discuss findings that could shape a future model law on AI oversight.

headline: QBE reshuffles Asia leadership with new COO and data/AI chief
summary: QBE named Patrick Karlowski as Chief Operating Officer for Asia, succeeding Klaas Dijkstra who moves to a Chief Information Officer role, while Florence Chan was appointed Head of Data, Analytics and AI for Asia, both based in Hong Kong.

headline: PBM giant MedImpact bulks up its risk-management arm with two acquisitions
summary: MedImpact, one of the largest independent U.S. pharmacy benefit managers, acquired two employer stop-loss and risk-management firms to broaden its offerings for self-funded employer health plans.

headline: India's Plum raises $20 million to scale its corporate health-insurance platform
summary: Bengaluru-based employee health-benefits startup Plum raised about ₹193 crore ($20.6M) in a Series B led by Peak XV Partners to expand its claims platform, AI-driven processing, and preventive-care services across its 600,000-plus covered lives.

headline: Insurers lean harder on AI for prior authorization as doctors cry foul over denials
summary: A growing bloc of payers has pledged to make at least 80% of prior-authorization decisions in real time by 2027 using AI, even as most physicians surveyed by the AMA say unchecked algorithmic review is driving up denial rates.

headline: CMS issues national playbook for new Medicaid work requirements
summary: CMS released nationwide implementation guidance for its Medicaid work-requirement rule, with states such as Arkansas and Montana beginning rollout in July 2026 ahead of a federal deadline; the agency projects about 2.3 million people will lose coverage.

headline: New York issues consumer guidance as Essential Plan eligibility narrows
summary: New York's Attorney General published guidance for residents after federal rule changes stripped Essential Plan eligibility from roughly 450,000 lawfully present immigrants and higher-income enrollees effective July 2026.

headline: Centene overhauls leadership and offers buyouts as ACA losses bite
summary: After shedding more than two million ACA exchange members, insurer Centene restructured its executive ranks and offered companywide voluntary buyouts in an effort to cut costs.

headline: Private medical cover in Britain hits its highest level since the financial crisis
summary: Roughly one in eight Britons now holds private medical insurance, the highest share since 2008, as frustration with NHS waiting times pushes more households and employers toward private cover.

headline: Asia-Pacific braces for the world's steepest medical cost inflation
summary: A global WTW survey of insurers found APAC medical costs are expected to climb about 14% in 2026 (nearly 17% in Singapore), led by cancer and cardiovascular claims, with most insurers expecting elevated cost trends to persist for years.

headline: Sutter Health and Allina Health lock in $26 billion merger agreement
summary: California-based Sutter Health and Minnesota-based Allina Health signed a definitive agreement to combine into a 39-hospital nonprofit system spanning three states, with Sutter committing $2 billion toward Allina's Upper Midwest operations.

headline: Wearable maker Whoop triples its valuation to $10 billion ahead of an IPO
summary: Fitness-tracking company Whoop raised $575 million in a Series G round backed by sovereign wealth funds and celebrity investors, tripling its valuation as its CEO signaled an IPO is the company's next step.

headline: Singapore to merge three separate hospital apps into one national health app
summary: Singapore's public healthcare clusters announced they will unify the NHG, NUHS and SingHealth patient apps into a single enhanced HealthHub app launching in November 2026, aiming to cut digital fragmentation for patients.

headline: CMS proposes 2027 hospital payment rule pushing more care into outpatient settings
summary: CMS released its CY2027 Hospital Outpatient and Ambulatory Surgical Center proposed rule, expanding site-neutral payment policy and other measures meant to curb Medicare spending and steer procedures toward lower-cost sites of care.

headline: Hospital CEO exits jump 32% as long-tenured leaders finally step aside
summary: Hospital and health-system CEO departures rose sharply in early 2026 versus the prior year, with veteran leaders including Mayo Clinic's Gianrico Farrugia and Yale New Haven Health's Christopher O'Connor announcing they are stepping down.

headline: India's hospital chains race to add capacity as Fortis breaks into Odisha
summary: Fortis Healthcare is building its first Odisha hospital, a roughly 300-bed, ₹500-crore tertiary care centre, part of a broader capacity expansion in which Apollo, Max and Fortis are together adding thousands of new beds nationwide.

headline: Sixth Street to become majority shareholder of pan-European life consolidator Monument Re
summary: Sixth Street signed a definitive agreement to acquire a majority stake in Monument Re, with Hannover Re remaining a key shareholder, giving the in-force life and annuity consolidator fresh capital for its European growth strategy.

headline: Standard Insurance exits individual annuity sales, shifts book to Pacific Guardian Life
summary: The Standard signed a definitive agreement to transition its individual annuities business to Pacific Guardian Life so it can concentrate on workplace benefits, with the deal expected to close in early 2027 pending regulatory approval.

headline: Jackson named InvestmentNews' 2026 Annuities Provider of the Year
summary: Jackson National Life won the award after launching a third and fourth generation RILA suite and a new fixed-indexed annuity with an embedded guaranteed withdrawal benefit, alongside a 14th straight year of top customer-service honors.

headline: Prudential adopts Hueler Income Solutions to add a 'personal pension' option to its own 401(k)
summary: Prudential Insurance Company of America began offering Hueler's Income Solutions platform inside its own retirement savings plan, letting participants convert a portion of savings into a self-funded annuity-based income stream.

headline: Insurance investment outsourcing tops $5.5 trillion in third-party AUM as APAC allocations surge
summary: Third-party general-account assets under management placed with outside managers grew 23% year-on-year, with private insurance AUM more than doubling since 2021 to $947 billion as insurers chase private fixed income capabilities.

headline: Law firm maps shifting regulatory landscape for insurer private-credit investments
summary: A new legal overview details how state insurance regulators are adapting capital and disclosure rules as insurers keep expanding into private credit and other alternative assets within their general accounts.

headline: Wealth Enhancement to absorb 88-year-old New York advisory dynasty Shufro-Glass in $760M deal
summary: Wealth Enhancement agreed to acquire the Shufro-Glass Group of Shufro Rose, adding more than $760 million in client assets and pushing the national RIA's total client assets above $157 billion once the deal closes in August.

headline: Aspen Standard Wealth adds $1.3B Michigan RIA CWS Financial Advisors in its eighth deal
summary: The PE-backed RIA aggregator acquired Kalamazoo-based CWS Financial Advisors, which will keep its fee-only structure while joining the platform, pushing Aspen's total affiliated assets to $15 billion.

headline: Clearstead adds $2.6B Philadelphia wealth team from myCIO Wealth Partners
summary: Cleveland-based Clearstead, backed by Flexpoint Ford, closed its acquisition of a nine-person Philadelphia team managing $2.6 billion in assets, marking its second deal above $2 billion so far this year.

headline: Orion becomes one of the first wealthtech firms to earn ISO/IEC 42001 AI-management certification
summary: The portfolio accounting provider passed an independent audit of the AI Management System governing its Denali AI layer, joining a small group of roughly 100-150 organizations worldwide with the AI governance certification.

headline: US RIA M&A already tops $100 billion in deal volume in 2026
summary: Registered investment advisor dealmaking is running at a record pace this year, with private equity-backed consolidators and mid-market mergers driving volume well past the $100 billion mark before mid-year.

headline: July property reinsurance renewals soften further as capital keeps flowing in
summary: Guy Carpenter reported that abundant reinsurance capital pushed July 1 property renewals toward double-digit rate reductions, continuing a cedent-favorable trend from mid-year renewals.

headline: US P&C insurers post $15.8B underwriting gain in Q1 2026, reversing year-ago loss
summary: Private US property/casualty insurers swung to a first-quarter underwriting profit of $15.8 billion, a sharp reversal from an $864 million underwriting loss in the same period last year.

headline: Hyperscale data center boom strains property insurance capacity
summary: A construction wave of AI-driven data centers is testing insurers' appetite for large, complex property risk, pushing some carriers toward securitization structures to manage concentrated exposure.

headline: MGAA sets 2026 priorities and confirms new board directors from Lloyd's, Aviva and member MGAs
summary: The Managing General Agents' Association outlined plans to expand member value and delegated-underwriting training, naming new elected and appointed directors including leaders from Lloyd's, Aviva and Optio Group.

headline: Arrow Global acquires specialist MGA Fusion Specialty Group
summary: Pan-European investment manager Arrow Global bought MGA Fusion Specialty Group through its insurance unit, adding an established London-market underwriting franchise to its growing MGA platform.

headline: ALKEME Insurance acquires specialty MGA Virtue Risk Partners
summary: US brokerage ALKEME Insurance bought New York-based MGA Virtue Risk Partners, which underwrites casualty and environmental specialty coverage for contractors, consultants and engineers nationwide.

headline: Aon names Tracy-Lee Kus co-CEO of EMEA in regional leadership shake-up
summary: Aon appointed Tracy-Lee Kus, previously CEO of its Global Broking Center, as co-CEO for EMEA covering the UK, Ireland, South Africa and the Middle East, part of a wider restructuring of its regional leadership.

headline: Fiduciary Services Group acquires Florida TPA Pension Investors Corporation
summary: The parent of DWC – The 401(k) Experts bought the 40-year-old Florida third-party administrator, adding roughly 900 retirement plans and deepening FSG's presence across the Southeast.

headline: Principal Financial Group agrees to acquire employee-benefits TPA Beam Benefits
summary: Principal said it will acquire Beam Benefits, which administers employee benefits for more than 25,000 small businesses, to strengthen its position in the small and midsized business segment.

headline: Zhibao Technology extends embedded insurance to Chengdu's Tianfu Citizen's Cloud platform
summary: Zhibao's brokerage subsidiary launched a beta deployment putting embedded insurance products in front of more than 20 million new users through a Chinese municipal digital-services platform.

headline: Insurers described as facing an 'agility crisis' as risk outpaces response speed
summary: An industry analysis argues insurers face a widening gap between how quickly climate, cyber and economic risks are changing and how quickly carriers can adjust pricing and products in response.

headline: Insurance broker software market valued at $1.96B in 2026 as AI reshapes servicing
summary: The insurance broker technology market is growing at a 7.9% CAGR as AI raises the capability floor for lead qualification, quote turnaround, client servicing and renewals.

headline: Honeycomb Insurance raises $40M to expand AI-powered real estate underwriting
summary: The digital insurer, which prices apartment and condo buildings without physical inspections using geospatial and aerial data, raised a round led by Zeev Ventures that brings its total funding to $95 million.

headline: CMS finalizes 2026 Medicare Advantage and Part D payment updates, raising plan payments 5.06%
summary: CMS's final Calendar Year 2026 rate announcement increases average payments to Medicare Advantage plans while average monthly premiums are expected to fall slightly to about $14, with supplemental benefits holding stable.

headline: UnitedHealthcare and Humana both exit more Medicare Advantage counties than they enter in 2026
summary: The two largest Medicare Advantage insurers are pulling back geographic footprint even as enrollment overall keeps growing, with UnitedHealthcare exiting 225 counties and Humana exiting 198 amid margin pressure.

headline: Congress's PBM reform law starts delinking compensation from drug prices as FTC presses Express Scripts and Caremark
summary: The Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2026 will base Medicare Part D PBM pay on flat service fees rather than rebates starting 2028 and bans Medicaid spread pricing, while the FTC's Express Scripts settlement is expected to cut patient drug costs by up to $7 billion over a decade.

headline: ACA marketplace premiums set for steepest jump since 2018 as enhanced subsidies lapse
summary: Insurers are proposing a median 18% rate increase for 2026 ACA marketplace plans as enhanced premium tax credits expire, a change expected to more than double what subsidized enrollees pay out of pocket and shrink enrollment by up to 4.8 million people.

headline: Sutter Health and Allina Health sign definitive agreement for $26B nonprofit merger
summary: The combination would create a 39-hospital system spanning California, Wisconsin and Minnesota serving more than five million patients, with Sutter pledging a $2 billion investment in Allina's Upper Midwest markets.

headline: UPMC signs definitive agreement to acquire CommonSpirit's Trinity Health System in Ohio
summary: UPMC will take over Trinity Health System's hospitals and clinics in the Ohio Valley, marking UPMC's first entry into Ohio, with the deal expected to close in fall 2026 pending regulatory approval.

headline: Health systems report major time savings from ambient AI documentation tools
summary: Intermountain Health cut time spent on visit notes by 27% and Cooper University Healthcare saved clinicians over an hour daily using Microsoft's Dragon Copilot, while MUSC's voice-AI platform now handles about a quarter of patient-access calls.

headline: LIC Pushes RBI and SEBI for New Long-Duration Instruments as Annuity Liabilities Balloon
summary: Life Insurance Corporation of India's leadership said the insurer is engaging the central bank and market regulator to create longer-tenor investment instruments capable of matching annuity liabilities that stretch 30 to 50 years, as annuity demand from NPS retirees rises.

headline: Empower to Pay $340 Million for Milliman's Retirement and Benefits Administration Business
summary: Empower agreed to acquire Milliman's retirement plan and benefits administration unit for $340 million, adding roughly 790,000 DB participants and 750,000 DC participants along with $130 billion in combined assets under administration and over 800 Milliman staff.

headline: India Extends New NPS Investment Options to Central Autonomous Body Employees
summary: The Indian government widened National Pension System investment choices, including a Life Cycle-75 High option and an Aggressive Life Cycle Fund, to employees of central autonomous bodies, letting subscribers pick strategies matched to their risk appetite and retirement horizon.

headline: Korea's National Pension Service Pivots From Fund Commitments to Direct Deals
summary: South Korea's National Pension Service is reducing reliance on blind-pool fund commitments in favor of direct real estate investments and club deals, reflecting a broader trend among large APAC retirement funds toward greater control over capital deployment.

headline: Four in Ten Insurers Now Use AI in Underwriting Amid Competitive and Pricing Pressure
summary: A Sollers Consulting analysis found underwriting has become the fastest-growing IT investment area for insurers, with roughly 40% now using AI in the function as carriers race to automate submission triage and unstructured document processing amid a softening market.

headline: Australian Pension Funds Post Single-Digit Returns for the Latest Financial Year
summary: Australia's A$4.5 trillion superannuation industry is reporting fiscal-year results with major funds like Australian Retirement Trust expecting default high-growth returns of about 9%, below the prior year's pace as markets cooled.

headline: Waverly Advisors Extends Trust Platform With $3 Billion Smithfield Trust Deal
summary: RIA aggregator Waverly Advisors closed its 34th acquisition since 2021, adding Pittsburgh-based Smithfield Trust Company and roughly $3 billion in fiduciary and trust assets to broaden its estate and trust administration capabilities in Pennsylvania.

headline: AI-Native Wealth Startup Arca Emerges From Stealth With $64 Million
summary: Advisor-led wealth manager Arca, which pairs human advisors with AI-driven automation and already oversees more than $1 billion in client assets, disclosed a combined $64 million seed and Series A raise led by General Catalyst and Venrock.

headline: Global Commercial Insurance Rates Fall as Property Softening Outweighs US Casualty Pressure
summary: Marsh's latest Global Insurance Market Index shows worldwide commercial insurance rates dropping about 5% in the second quarter, driven by steep declines in property pricing that more than offset continued rate increases in US casualty lines.

headline: GEICO Completes Leadership Overhaul With New CFO Hire
summary: GEICO named David Foy, a former White Mountains Insurance Group finance chief, as its new CFO, rounding out the senior leadership team Berkshire Hathaway installed at the auto insurer under CEO Nancy Pierce.

headline: Roadzen to Buy European Car-Rental Insurance MGA for $15 Million
summary: Nasdaq-listed insurtech Roadzen signed a deal to acquire a technology-driven European MGA focused on short-term car rental insurance, adding roughly 800,000 policies a year and AI-based underwriting and claims tools to its platform.

headline: Convex Launches Tech-Enabled MGA Kinetic Insurance Services
summary: Specialty insurer Convex Group unveiled Kinetic Insurance Services, a new wholly owned, technology-enabled MGA targeting specialty and niche lines that will begin trading in the fourth quarter of 2026, backed by Convex and third-party capacity.

headline: MDIndia TPA Opens Fifth Chennai Claims Hub as South India Volumes Grow
summary: MDIndia Health Insurance TPA has launched a new claims-processing center of excellence in Chennai, growing local headcount past 450 staff and adding over 120 claims-review doctors as it deepens its 23-branch Tamil Nadu network.

headline: New Federal Rules Would Force TPAs to Disclose Compensation on Self-Funded Plans
summary: A Department of Labor proposal, converging with 2026 appropriations-law changes, would require pharmacy benefit managers and the third-party administrators contracting with them to give employer plan sponsors detailed upfront and semiannual compensation disclosures for plan years beginning July 1, 2026.

headline: Embedded Insurance and Finance Draw Closer Regulatory Scrutiny as Sector Matures
summary: As insurance and financial products embedded directly into everyday apps and checkouts move from novelty to mainstream, regulators including the UK's FCA are moving to extend open-finance data-sharing rules to cover insurance, pensions, lending and savings.

headline: Goldman Sachs Leads $110 Million Round for AI Decisioning Startup Taktile
summary: Taktile, whose agentic AI platform automates high-stakes underwriting, claims and fraud decisions for banks and insurers, raised a $110 million Series C led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives with Tiger Global and other backers, bringing total funding to $184 million.

headline: Reliance Global Taps Ex-Coinbase, Capital One Executive as CTO for AI Agency Roll-Up
summary: Insurance agency consolidator Reliance Global Group named a new Chief Technology Officer with a Coinbase and Capital One background, alongside a new COO and EVP, to lead development of AI-native insurance products and its agency acquisition strategy.

headline: Agentic AI Platform mea Reports Broker Productivity Gains Across 20-Country Rollout
summary: Insurance operations platform mea says insurers, brokers and MGAs using its agentic AI tools for underwriting, claims and broking are seeing roughly 30% higher broker productivity and 40% more underwriting capacity across more than 30 live deployments processing over $400 billion in premium.

headline: French health insurtech Alan closes €480 million Series G, valuing it at €5.5 billion
summary: Prosus led the round alongside existing backers Index Ventures and Teachers' Venture Growth plus new investor Dara Holdings, making it one of Europe's largest insurtech raises this year as Alan pushes into prevention-focused health coverage globally.

headline: Paris-based Panora raises $5 million to bring AI tooling to European insurance brokers
summary: The seed round, led by Isai with Kima Ventures and others participating, will fund software that automates policy comparison and administrative work for brokerages across Europe.

headline: Singapore's Igloo acquires Eazy Digital in its second Thailand deal within a year
summary: The acquisition folds Eazy Digital's client base and Bangkok team into Igloo, with its founder becoming Igloo's Thailand country head, extending Igloo's push into Southeast Asian digital distribution amid regional insurance reform.

headline: Health insurer stocks climb as Wall Street braces for a closely watched Q2 2026 earnings season
summary: Investors are watching CVS and peers for signs of whether the industry can sustain the earnings beats and raised guidance most major insurers delivered in Q1, after medical cost ratios came in better than analysts feared.

headline: PBM trade group launches its largest-ever ad campaign as reform pressure builds in Washington
summary: The Pharmaceutical Care Management Association unveiled a seven-figure lobbying and advertising push framing drugmakers as the affordability problem, countering momentum for PBM reform following Congress's February legislation delinking PBM pay from drug list prices.

headline: One in ten Medicare Advantage members forced off their plan for 2026 as insurers retreat from markets
summary: A new study finds forced disenrollments hit roughly 10% of MA enrollees heading into 2026, a tenfold jump from historical norms, as carriers pulled back from unprofitable counties and plans.

headline: Three-quarters of US health systems now use or are piloting AI platforms, survey finds
summary: Half of respondents run three or more AI applications, and more than half of those able to measure ROI report at least a 2x return, with documentation, imaging triage and virtual nursing among the leading use cases.

headline: NHS logs its busiest-ever month as heatwaves and World Cup crowds push A&E demand to record highs
summary: Average daily A&E attendances topped 81,000 for the first time in June as temperatures hit nearly 38C, with NHS leaders warning that summer is now straining the health service as much as winter historically has.

headline: Sutter Health and Allina Health sign definitive deal to form a $26 billion nonprofit system
summary: The combination would create a 39-hospital network spanning California and the Upper Midwest, with Allina retaining its brand as a regional division and Sutter committing over $2 billion in new investment for Minnesota and Wisconsin facilities.

headline: MultiCare and Samaritan Health boards approve affiliation creating an 18-hospital Pacific Northwest system
summary: The deal gives Tacoma-based MultiCare its first acute-care presence in Oregon and comes with a 10-year commitment to modernize Samaritan's facilities and expand telehealth, pending state regulatory review expected to conclude this summer.

headline: Corebridge and Equitable agree to $22 billion all-stock merger
summary: Corebridge Financial and Equitable Holdings will combine in an all-stock deal valued near $22 billion, creating a combined retirement, life insurance and asset management platform with roughly $1.5 trillion in assets under management and administration. The merged company will operate under the Equitable name and trade under ticker EQH, with closing expected by year-end 2026.

headline: India's life insurers post 16% retail premium growth in June
summary: India's life insurance sector logged a 16% year-on-year jump in retail premiums for June 2026, led by state-owned LIC's 21% gain, while private insurers ICICI Prudential and SBI Life also posted strong double-digit growth in new business.

headline: India moves to let a cooperative-sector company sell life insurance
summary: India's cooperation minister said the government will facilitate a new cooperative-sector life insurer now that a legal change has removed a prior capital barrier, even as overall life insurance penetration has slipped for a third straight year.

headline: ICICI Prudential debuts India's first guaranteed-maturity ULIP
summary: ICICI Prudential Life launched ICICI Pru Signature Secure, billed as the Indian industry's first unit-linked insurance plan with a built-in guaranteed maturity benefit of up to 140% of premium paid, alongside life cover and no allocation charges.

headline: UK bulk annuity market on pace for record £70 billion in 2026
summary: The Association of British Insurers has stood up a new pensions board to focus on defined-benefit risk transfer and bulk annuity activity, as total UK pension risk transferred to insurers is projected to climb roughly 15% this year with more large scheme deals expected.

headline: Life insurers push AI deeper into underwriting decisions
summary: Carriers are increasingly automating life underwriting tasks, with reporting suggesting straight-through processing rates have jumped sharply and standard policy decisions can now be reached in minutes rather than days, though most gains so far come from speed rather than improved risk selection.

headline: Insurers' private credit bets grow even as default rates climb
summary: Life insurers now represent roughly a quarter of private credit capital providers, with holdings up more than 20% in 2025 to about a tenth of total assets, but rising defaults in the asset class are drawing closer regulatory scrutiny of the exposure.

headline: DOL proposes safe harbor clearing path for private assets in 401(k)s
summary: The Department of Labor proposed a process-based safe harbor under ERISA that would give plan fiduciaries a clearer, presumption-of-prudence route to include alternative investments such as private equity, real estate and infrastructure in participant-directed retirement plan lineups.

headline: Large 401(k) plans increasingly adopt automatic account portability
summary: Adoption of auto-portability, which automatically moves small balances into a new employer's plan when workers change jobs, is accelerating among large 401(k) plans in 2026, with adopting plans now covering more than 6.6 million active participants.

headline: India's pension body to launch bundled pension-and-health NPS product
summary: PFRDA plans to roll out 'NPS Swasthya' within roughly two months, a scheme pairing a pension account with top-up health insurance coverage, with Aditya Birla Health Insurance signed on as the first participating insurer.

headline: Supreme Court to weigh benchmark standard in 401(k) fee lawsuits
summary: The US Supreme Court agreed to hear Anderson v. Intel, a case that will decide whether ERISA fiduciary-breach claims over fund underperformance must point to a 'meaningful benchmark,' with a ruling likely to shape litigation risk just as regulators open the door to alternative investments in plans.

headline: Pension risk transfer buy-ins hit record as plan sponsors de-risk
summary: US pension buy-in transactions reached roughly $17.5 billion across 17 deals in 2025 as the structure moved from a niche tool for mega-plans to a mainstream de-risking step, part of an overall $48.7 billion pension risk transfer market tracked by Aon.

headline: CVC closes takeover of credit specialist Marathon Asset Management
summary: Private equity firm CVC completed its acquisition of Marathon Asset Management, which will be rebranded CVC Marathon, extending CVC's push into private credit and broadening its alternative asset management footprint.

headline: Target-date fund assets swell to $4.8 trillion as CITs take the lead
summary: The US target-date fund market grew over 20% to roughly $4.8 trillion, with collective investment trusts now holding the majority of assets ahead of mutual funds and five firms, led by Vanguard, controlling about 80% of the market.

headline: Brookfield Asset Management installs Connor Teskey as CEO
summary: Brookfield Asset Management named Connor Teskey chief executive effective February 2026, with longtime leader Bruce Flatt stepping back to chair the board and continuing as CEO of parent Brookfield Corporation.

headline: APG Asset Management's chief executive to depart after two decades
summary: Ronald Wuijster is stepping down as CEO of Dutch pension investor APG Asset Management, with an interim successor taking over responsibilities from March 2026 pending regulatory approval, marking the end of a near 20-year tenure.

headline: APAC wealth and asset management assets set to keep outpacing the West
summary: PwC's Asia-Pacific asset and wealth management report shows Singapore and Hong Kong AUM each nearing $4.5-4.6 trillion, with regional assets projected to reach $34.5 trillion by 2030, growing faster than North America or Europe.

headline: SEC and CFTC move to slash private fund reporting requirements
summary: The two regulators jointly proposed raising Form PF filing thresholds, eliminating quarterly private-equity event reporting, and easing hedge fund exposure reporting, a rollback aimed at cutting compliance burden for private fund managers.

headline: AI investment-management platform Moment raises $78 million as adoption surges among large wealth firms
summary: Moment closed a $78 million Series C led by Index Ventures just months after its prior round, with its AI operating system now used by wealth firms collectively overseeing more than $10 trillion, up from about $300 billion roughly 18 months earlier.

headline: Global wealthtech investment sinks 67% year-over-year even as deal count climbs
summary: Wealthtech startups worldwide raised roughly $932 million across 151 deals in the second quarter of 2026, a sharp drop in dollars from a year earlier despite a 10% rise in deal volume, with the US capturing about half of the period's top ten rounds.

headline: New federal bill would let RIA clients qualify as accredited investors through their advisor relationship
summary: Proposed legislation, the Informed Investor Access Act, would let clients of registered investment advisors be treated as accredited investors, opening access to private markets and drawing praise from wealth management trade groups.

headline: LPL Financial keeps recruiting streak alive with a $6 billion hybrid RIA and two advisor teams
summary: LPL Financial added a roughly $6 billion hybrid RIA along with two additional advisor teams managing hundreds of millions in assets, underscoring intense competition among broker-dealer platforms for breakaway advisors.

headline: India's wealth management industry eyes $1.7 trillion by 2030 even as fiduciary advisor supply stays thin
summary: India's asset and wealth management market is projected to nearly double by 2030 on retail financialization and digital infrastructure, but the country still has fewer than 1,000 SEBI-registered investment advisors serving over 200 million investors.

headline: Wealthtech leaders sketch out how AI will reshape advisor tools next
summary: Ten wealthtech executives and investors weighed in on where artificial intelligence is headed in wealth management, pointing to next-best-action recommendations, planning alerts and risk flags as the next wave of features advisors will adopt.

headline: NAIC research arm examines how AI is reshaping insurance regulation
summary: The NAIC's Center for Insurance Policy and Research hosted a webinar dissecting a new academic paper on artificial intelligence and insurance regulation, part of the association's continued scrutiny of insurer AI and big-data use.

headline: AI-native landlord insurer Honeycomb raises $40 million to expand no-inspection underwriting
summary: Honeycomb Insurance, which underwrites apartment buildings and condo associations using an AI-driven, no-inspection model, raised a $40 million round led by Zeev Ventures after exiting 2025 with $275 million in written premium.

headline: NOAA issues most favorable Atlantic hurricane forecast in over a decade
summary: NOAA's 2026 outlook puts a 55% chance on a below-normal Atlantic hurricane season, the first such forecast since 2015, though insurers say a single landfalling storm could still drive major losses and are holding firm on coastal deductibles.

headline: US commercial insurance market splits in two as property rates crater and casualty keeps hardening
summary: Commercial property pricing fell a record 7.1% in the first quarter of 2026 on abundant capacity, while casualty lines including commercial auto kept seeing high-single to double-digit rate increases amid persistent social inflation.

headline: Gallagher expands wholesale reach with acquisition of Kansas MGA Med James
summary: Arthur J. Gallagher's Risk Placement Services wholesale unit acquired Overland Park-based Med James, a managing general agency and wholesale broker, extending Gallagher's binding-authority footprint in the North Central US.

headline: Gallagher buys Western Canada retail brokerage Wilson M. Beck
summary: Arthur J. Gallagher acquired Burnaby, British Columbia-based Wilson M. Beck Insurance Services, adding a commercial brokerage with construction, real estate and hospitality specialties to its Canadian retail operations.

headline: Pay-per-mile MGA Mile Auto buys 60-year-old agency partner Insurance House
summary: Tech-enabled auto MGA Mile Auto acquired Georgia-based Insurance House, combining AI-driven, mileage-based underwriting with six decades of independent-agency relationships to create a nearly $100 million premium platform across 10 states.

headline: UK's MGA trade body names Bspoke's Tim Smyth as new chairman
summary: The Managing General Agents' Association appointed Tim Smyth, who recently sold Bspoke Group to NFP (an Aon company), as its new chairman, succeeding Charles Manchester after his decade-long tenure.

headline: India's GIFT City rolls out new MGA licensing regime for foreign insurers
summary: The International Financial Services Centres Authority introduced a regulatory framework allowing managing general agents to operate for foreign insurers out of GIFT City, a move industry figures are calling a pivotal build-or-broker decision point for Indian insurance distribution.

headline: Private equity now owns more than 30% of US managing general agents
summary: Private equity firms are increasingly targeting MGAs as a growth platform because the fee-based, asset-light model scales without heavy capital requirements, with PE ownership now exceeding three in ten MGA entities in the US.

headline: Alternative capital and ILS funds increasingly back US MGA growth
summary: A growing share of US managing general agents are turning to insurance-linked securities and other alternative capital rather than traditional reinsurers to fund underwriting capacity, according to Conning research highlighted by Gallagher Re.

headline: Specialty MGA Amiga taps veteran underwriter to lead new Hong Kong financial lines push
summary: Amiga Specialty appointed longtime cyber, D&O and professional-liability underwriter Ralph Sherbahn to lead its newly launched Hong Kong operation as it builds out financial-lines coverage across Asia Pacific.

headline: Health-plan infrastructure startup Yuzu Health lands $35 million to modernize TPA operations
summary: Yuzu Health closed a Series A led by General Catalyst and Chemistry to expand its platform for claims processing, eligibility and stop-loss administration, having already processed over $1 billion in claims across all 50 states.

headline: Commentary questions whether AI will sideline traditional TPAs entirely
summary: An industry op-ed argues that while AI is projected to automate the bulk of routine claims handling, TPAs are more likely to shift toward complex-case oversight and care coordination than disappear outright.

headline: Private equity keeps consolidating the claims-services and TPA sector
summary: An advisory firm's analysis finds deal activity accelerating in claims services and TPAs as PE-backed platforms approach exit windows and buyers chase firms with complex-claims and adjacent-service capabilities, squeezing smaller independents toward sale.

headline: AI-focused startups grabbed almost all insurtech venture funding in Q1
summary: Gallagher Re's latest report shows global insurtech investment held at roughly $1.63 billion in the first quarter of 2026, with AI-centered companies capturing about 95% of the dollars and average deal sizes hitting multi-year highs.

headline: Study projects India's insurtech sector nearing $1 billion in fresh funding
summary: A joint industry report forecasts private investment into Indian insurtech topping $1 billion over the next year as the market shifts from agent-led sales toward platform-driven, data-based distribution.

headline: Flood-forecasting insurtech Previsico taps new CEO to push into the US
summary: The Loughborough University spinout named Mark Trumper, formerly of Axco Insurance Information, as chief executive to lead its next phase of international expansion.

headline: BrokerTech Ventures sets September Chicago summit, spotlights new broker-focused VC fund
summary: BrokerTech Ventures announced its second annual BrokerTech Connect conference and highlighted the BrokerTech Fund, a venture vehicle built with ManchesterStory specifically for startups serving insurance brokers and wholesalers.

headline: Cara pulls in $8 million seed round to automate brokerage back-office work
summary: The AI platform for insurance brokerages, backed by Stripe's former COO and other tech veterans, says it reached seven-figure annual revenue within seven months by automating proposals, certificates and client communications.

headline: Outmarket AI raises $17 million to grow its insurance distribution platform
summary: The funding will let Outmarket AI expand its product aimed at helping agencies and brokers scale marketing and sales operations, part of a wave of AI-focused broker-tooling raises in 2026.

headline: Sixfold brings its AI underwriting assistant to the broader P&C market
summary: After three years of development with major carriers, Sixfold made its AI Underwriter generally available to property and casualty insurers, aiming to speed submission review and risk triage.

headline: Digital insurance distributor Turtlemint prices IPO to raise roughly $106 million
summary: Turtlemint FinTech Solutions opened its Indian public offering, combining a fresh share issue and offer-for-sale, as its tech-enabled 'phygital' broker-advisor model targets continued growth in a still-underpenetrated market.

headline: Insurity deepens insurtech partnership with OIP for AI-driven document processing
summary: Insurity is expanding its multi-year partnership with OIP Insurtech, broadening the AI-enabled document intelligence and system-integration services it delivers to insurance carriers.

headline: Lloyd's underwriter Carbon lands growth equity backing from FTV Capital
summary: London-based delegated authority specialist Carbon Underwriting, which runs Lloyd's Syndicate 4747, secured a significant growth-equity investment from FTV Capital to fund its Graphene data/AI platform and US expansion, with earlier backer Apiary Capital exiting.

headline: US insurtechs pull in $420 million in January as mega-rounds return
summary: Global insurtech funding rebounded to roughly $420 million in January 2026, driven largely by a handful of large US-based deals, according to Fintech Global's tracking data.

headline: Insurtech investment climbs to $1.63 billion in Q1 2026 as AI dominates deal flow
summary: CB Insights data shows global insurtech investment rose about 27% year-over-year to $1.63 billion in Q1 2026, with AI-branded startups capturing a record 95%-plus share of the capital.

headline: Insurtech Insights 2026 shows industry moving from 'what is AI' to deployment questions
summary: At the 2026 Insurtech Insights conference, discussion shifted from explaining artificial intelligence to debating how agentic AI is actually being rolled out across underwriting and claims, along with real operational growing pains.

headline: Asia-Pacific insurtech market on track for nearly five-fold growth by 2035
summary: Industry forecasts put the Asia-Pacific insurtech market at roughly $28 billion in 2026, projected to grow about 19% annually to over $138 billion by 2035, powered by digital-first adoption across China, India, Japan and South Korea.

headline: Nearly half of US states now follow NAIC's AI model bulletin as insurers race to deploy AI
summary: As AI becomes embedded in underwriting, pricing and claims handling, 23 states plus Washington D.C. have adopted the NAIC's model bulletin governing insurers' AI use, with a national AI evaluation tool now piloting across a dozen states.

headline: FTC secures landmark Express Scripts settlement expected to cut insulin costs by billions
summary: The FTC settled its insulin-pricing lawsuit against Express Scripts, forcing the PBM to stop favoring high-list-price drugs on formularies, delink compensation from negotiated savings, and boost transparency — changes projected to save patients up to $7 billion over a decade.

headline: Congress enacts sweeping PBM reform bill delinking pay from drug prices
summary: New federal legislation passed in early 2026 bars PBMs from earning compensation tied to drug prices or rebates in Medicare Part D starting 2028, bans Medicaid spread pricing, and adds annual data-transparency requirements to HHS.

headline: UnitedHealth's profit tops $6 billion in Q1 as medical costs ease and guidance rises
summary: UnitedHealth Group posted Q1 2026 earnings per share of $7.23 on revenue of $111.7 billion, beating estimates, and raised its full-year 2026 profit guidance as medical cost trends moderated.

headline: CMS proposes new electronic prior-authorization mandate for drug coverage
summary: A newly proposed CMS interoperability rule would require payers to support electronic prior authorization for drugs, shrink decision-turnaround times, and publish more transparency data, extending prior-auth reform into pharmacy benefits.

headline: Long NHS waits push more Britons toward private medical insurance
summary: Persistent NHS waiting lists are driving increased UK consumer interest in private medical insurance, with buyers citing faster access to diagnostics and specialists as the main draw.

headline: Sutter Health moves to absorb Allina Health in $26 billion multi-state tie-up
summary: Sutter Health announced plans to acquire Minneapolis-based Allina Health, forming a combined nonprofit system spanning California, Minnesota and Wisconsin with 39 hospitals and roughly 88,000 employees, expected to close by year-end 2026.

headline: Stanford-Harvard report finds clinical AI hype colliding with real-world limits
summary: A joint Stanford-Harvard 'State of Clinical AI' report examines which AI tools are actually delivering value inside hospitals after a boom in pilots, highlighting gaps between vendor promises and clinical performance.

headline: Narayana Health to open India's first nurse-led 'smart' hospital in Bengaluru
summary: Narayana Health is building a new paperless, technology-enabled hospital in Bengaluru's Banashankari area that will be operationally run by nurses, part of an effort to groom nursing staff for future hospital leadership roles.

headline: Bed-blocking is costing the NHS an estimated 2.7 billion pounds a year
summary: Analysis finds delayed hospital discharges — with around 13,000 patients medically fit to leave remaining in NHS beds daily — are costing the health service roughly £2.7 billion annually, driven largely by social-care capacity shortfalls.

headline: Digital health funding enters a 'maturity era' in H1 2026 with fewer, bigger deals
summary: Galen Growth's H1 2026 digital health report finds capital increasingly concentrated in fewer, larger growth-stage rounds rather than spread across early-stage startups, alongside rising M&A exit value even as deal counts fell.

headline: MemorialCare taps new CEO as 24-year chief becomes executive chairman
summary: Longtime MemorialCare CEO Barry Arbuckle moved into the role of executive chairman effective July 1, handing the chief executive title to President David Kim after leading the Fountain Valley, California system for 24 years.

headline: Unum cedes $3.8 billion long-term care block to Fortitude Re
summary: Unum Life Insurance Company of America agreed to cede individual long-term care policies representing $3.8 billion of statutory reserves to Fortitude Reinsurance, which will retrocede the biometric risk to a global reinsurer while Unum keeps handling claims administration.

headline: US life/annuity industry income falls 18% as premiums drop $36 billion in Q1
summary: An early look at first-quarter 2026 results shows the U.S. life and annuity sector's total income declined 18% year-over-year as premiums and annuity considerations fell by roughly $36 billion industry-wide.

headline: Manulife overhauls executive leadership team, names Patrick Graham CEO of Manulife Canada
summary: Manulife Financial restructured its executive leadership team, appointing Patrick Graham as President and CEO of Manulife Canada as part of a broader realignment of senior roles across the insurer.

headline: Wall Street lobbies to loosen 401(k) investment rules
summary: Financial industry groups are pushing federal regulators to relax restrictions on what asset classes retirement plans can offer, a move critics warn could expose savers to less liquid, higher-fee private investments inside their 401(k)s.

headline: Target-date funds with built-in retirement income features surpass $100 billion
summary: Assets in target-date funds that embed guaranteed or systematic retirement-income features crossed $100 billion, as more defined-contribution plan sponsors adopt income-generating default options for near-retirees.

headline: Catastrophe bond market hits record $65.6 billion outstanding after blockbuster second quarter
summary: Total catastrophe bond and related insurance-linked securities issuance topped $16.1 billion year-to-date in 2026, with second-quarter issuance alone exceeding $11.3 billion across 48 transactions, pushing the outstanding market to a new high.

headline: RIA M&A on pace to set a new full-year record in 2026, Echelon projects
summary: Echelon's newly published RIA and Wealth Management M&A Multiples Report projects full-year 2026 deal volume will reach roughly 475 transactions, edging past 2025's record of 466 as consolidation among independent advisory firms continues.

headline: Vestmark's RIA advisory assets jump to $50 billion from $10 billion in 18 months
summary: Vestmark Advisory Services has grown the assets it manages for RIAs five-fold in a year and a half, crediting referral relationships with major asset managers and demand for its tax-overlay and direct-indexing technology.

headline: Women who work with a financial advisor report far higher retirement confidence
summary: New survey data cited in Kitces' weekend roundup found women working with a financial advisor are roughly 60% more likely to feel confident managing their finances, with retirement planning topping the list of areas where they seek professional help.

headline: US P&C industry posts $16.3 billion Q1 underwriting gain as catastrophe losses plunge
summary: The U.S. property and casualty industry swung to a $16.3 billion net underwriting gain in the first quarter of 2026, reversing a year-ago loss, as catastrophe losses fell to $10 billion from $33.3 billion a year earlier following the 2025 California wildfires.

headline: Reinsurers show more flexibility on structure and price at July 1 renewals
summary: Gallagher Re reports that reinsurers offered greater flexibility on contract structures and pricing at the mid-year renewal, as record capital continued to soften property catastrophe rates across most regions.

headline: Independent agents placed 62% of all US P&C premium in 2025, up from 61.5%
summary: The Big 'I' 2026 Market Share Report shows independent agents wrote 62% of all property/casualty premium in the U.S. last year, including 87.7% of commercial lines, extending the channel's steady gains over captive and direct distribution.

headline: Zurich launches dedicated life sciences insurance product across nine European countries
summary: Zurich is rolling out a specialist life sciences insurance product covering Belgium, Denmark, France, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland and the UK, joining Markel and QBE in a specialty segment brokers say few insurers fully understand.

headline: Global reinsurance capital reaches $790 billion even as premium growth stays muted
summary: Aon's mid-year Reinsurance Market Dynamics report finds industry capital hit a record $790 billion, but premium growth of just over 1% highlights a widening imbalance between abundant capacity and softer demand.

headline: Arrow Global Group agrees to acquire specialty MGA Fusion Specialty Group
summary: Arrow Global Group announced an agreement to acquire Fusion Specialty Group, a specialist managing general agent, in a deal expected to close in the third quarter of 2026 subject to regulatory approval.

headline: Gallagher's Risk Placement Services acquires Kansas MGA Med James
summary: Arthur J. Gallagher's wholesale brokerage unit Risk Placement Services acquired Med James, an Overland Park, Kansas-based managing general agency and wholesale broker focused on commercial and personal lines property/casualty risks.

headline: Acrisure launches 'Asero' brand to unify its specialty MGA businesses
summary: Acrisure unveiled Asero as a unified brand for its portfolio of specialty managing general agencies, aiming to present a single identity to carriers and brokers as it continues consolidating MGA acquisitions.

headline: Marsh names UK chief claims officer as Aon appoints new EMEA co-CEO
summary: Marsh appointed Helen Haggie as UK chief claims officer for Marsh Risk effective July 20, while Aon named Tracy-Lee Kus as one of its new co-chief executives for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

headline: Group Benefit Services acquires Sacramento third-party administrator Integrity Administrators
summary: Group Benefit Services acquired Integrity Administrators, a longstanding Sacramento-based TPA, aiming to combine its nurse-navigator support model with GBS's existing client base to improve service and cost savings.

headline: Blue Cross to return as third-party administrator for North Carolina's State Health Plan
summary: Blue Cross NC will resume serving as the third-party administrator for the North Carolina State Health Plan, which covers hundreds of thousands of state employees, teachers and retirees, following a new contract award.

headline: Zhibao Technology scales embedded insurance to nearly 20 million users via China smart-city partnership
summary: Zhibao Technology expanded its embedded insurance ecosystem through a partnership with Tianfu Citizen's Cloud, a Chengdu smart-city services platform, extending digital insurance access to nearly 20 million registered users.

headline: Jointly AI launches what it calls the first fully autonomous AI insurance broker platform
summary: Jointly AI unveiled an end-to-end autonomous brokerage platform for UK personal-lines insurance that uses voice AI to call providers, navigate phone menus, negotiate quotes and deliver results without human involvement.

headline: Hyperexponential launches agentic AI tool that turns broker submissions into priced quotes
summary: Hyperexponential introduced hyperoperator, an AI agent that moves commercial P&C broker submissions from initial intake to a decision-ready, priced file inside a carrier's existing pricing and authority controls — in one demo, pricing a cyber risk in under three minutes.

headline: Insurtech Openly secures growth funding and expands Allianz Re reinsurance partnership
summary: Homeowners insurtech Openly, which sells exclusively through independent agents, closed a growth funding round led by existing backers with new participation from Allianz X, alongside an expanded long-term reinsurance agreement with Allianz Re.

headline: Insurtech Pace raises $46 million Series B for AI-driven insurance operations
summary: Pace closed a $46 million Series B round to expand its AI agents for policy servicing, claims processing, renewals and submissions, adding to a wave of 2026 funding concentrated in AI-native insurance automation startups.

headline: CMS finalizes 2026 rule strengthening Medicare Advantage prior-authorization protections
summary: CMS's 2026 final rule requires Medicare Advantage plans to issue prior-authorization decisions within 72 hours for expedited requests and seven calendar days for standard requests, while also clarifying appeals processes for enrollees.

headline: ACA marketplace premiums jumped 58% in 2026 after enhanced subsidies expired
summary: Average ACA marketplace premiums rose 58% in 2026 as more generous pandemic-era subsidies lapsed, pushing more consumers into high-deductible bronze plans as total enrollment fell by 1.2 million to 23.1 million people.

headline: UnitedHealth's Q1 medical loss ratio beats expectations, prompting raised guidance
summary: UnitedHealth reported first-quarter 2026 revenue of $111.7 billion and a medical loss ratio of 83.9%, well below analyst expectations, and raised its full-year adjusted earnings guidance on strong medical cost management.

headline: Indian parliamentary panel calls for doubling Ayushman Bharat coverage to ₹10 lakh
summary: A parliamentary standing committee recommended raising the coverage cap under India's Ayushman Bharat public health insurance scheme from ₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh per family, citing the rising cost of complex procedures like organ transplants and cancer treatment.

headline: Baptist Health Arkansas set to close acquisition of Magnolia Regional Medical Center
summary: Baptist Health's transaction to acquire Magnolia Regional Medical Center was expected to close July 12, extending a run of hospital consolidation that has produced the strongest first-quarter deal count since 2020.

headline: IKS Health acquires health IT vendor TruBridge in $557 million deal
summary: IKS Health agreed to acquire TruBridge for $557 million, combining IKS's clinical documentation and revenue-cycle services with TruBridge's health IT platform as healthcare M&A activity remains elevated through 2026.

headline: Health systems map out their next phase of clinical AI adoption
summary: Health system leaders are shifting focus from isolated AI pilots to enterprise-wide priorities such as governance, workflow integration and measurable outcomes as clinical AI tools for imaging and diagnosis move toward wider deployment.

headline: Hospital and private-equity M&A activity expected to keep rising through 2026
summary: Hospital dealmaking is on track to accelerate further in 2026, with private equity playing a growing role alongside traditional health system mergers even as reimbursement and drug-pricing policy uncertainty persists.

headline: Corebridge and Equitable shareholders to vote on $22 billion merger this month
summary: Corebridge Financial and Equitable Holdings have scheduled special shareholder meetings for July 30 to approve their previously announced all-stock combination, which would create a retirement, life and asset management group with roughly $1.5 trillion in assets under the Equitable name.

headline: Annuity sales are on pace for another record-setting year
summary: Industry coverage points to U.S. annuity sales staying above $450 billion in 2026 after four straight record years, with fixed indexed annuities and in-plan lifetime-income products cited as key growth drivers.

headline: Regulators start eyeing the AI models baked into annuity pricing and sales
summary: A Forbes analysis describes growing regulatory attention on opaque AI systems insurers now use to price, underwrite and market annuities, warning that unmonitored model risk could create new consumer-protection exposures.

headline: Reinsurance Group of America promotes finance veteran to CFO
summary: RGA named Executive Vice President Laura Cockrill as chief financial officer effective immediately, succeeding Axel Andre, who is leaving the reinsurer; Cockrill has more than 25 years of experience across the company's finance functions.

headline: Pacific Life Re strikes third block reinsurance deal in Japan
summary: Pacific Life Re completed its third asset-intensive block reinsurance transaction with Tokio Marine & Nichido Anshin Life, covering in-force whole life policies and aimed at reducing the Japanese insurer's long-term interest-rate risk.

headline: Italy switches on immediate automatic pension enrollment for new hires
summary: As of July 1, Italy replaced its old six-month opt-in delay with automatic enrollment of newly hired private-sector workers into supplementary pension funds starting on their hire date, giving them 60 days to opt out instead.

headline: Direct lenders close some of the largest private credit funds on record in first-half 2026
summary: A first-half fundraising roundup shows managers including Barings, Crescent Capital, Churchill Asset Management and Blackstone closing multibillion-dollar direct-lending and credit vehicles, reflecting insurers' and institutions' rising appetite for private credit.

headline: MetLife flags softer variable investment income ahead of second-quarter results
summary: MetLife pre-announced that variable investment income for the quarter ended June 30 will likely come in between $220 million and $270 million pretax, tracking below its $1.6 billion full-year guidance pace, ahead of its August 5 earnings release.

headline: London-founded AI investing platform MDOTM lands $27 million to expand Sphere globally
summary: MDOTM closed a $27 million growth equity round led by Expedition Growth Capital to scale its AI-driven Sphere platform, which already supports over $100 billion in assets across 60-plus financial institutions including Morgan Stanley and Amundi. The raise brings the firm's total funding to roughly $36.5 million and will fund hiring in AI research and global expansion.

headline: Maybank rolls out AI-powered advisory tools built with Swiss fintech Evooq
summary: Malaysian banking group Maybank partnered with Switzerland-based Evooq to launch an AI advisory platform, Advisor Assist, giving relationship managers consolidated portfolio views, risk analytics and next-best-action recommendations. The rollout is part of Maybank's broader wealth transformation push as regional banks race to embed AI into advisory workflows.

headline: US RIA industry assets swell past $176 trillion as consolidation concentrates at the top
summary: New industry data shows registered investment advisers now manage a record $176.8 trillion in assets, a 22.3% jump, with record numbers of advisers and clients served. The report notes that 77% of RIA assets now sit with just 7% of firms, as mega-RIAs continue to scale largely through market appreciation and acquisitions rather than organic growth.

headline: Commercial P&C pricing keeps softening as capacity floods back into the market
summary: Commercial property and casualty rates continued to ease through mid-2026, with abundant reinsurance capacity and a quieter hurricane season driving double-digit rate decreases on many property placements. Commercial auto remains the notable exception, still facing upward pressure from social inflation and rising litigation and repair costs.

headline: UK insurers face crunch deadline to prove they can wind down safely
summary: The Prudential Regulation Authority's solvent exit planning regime became fully binding on 30 June 2026, requiring most PRA-regulated insurers to maintain a documented Solvent Exit Analysis showing how they could leave the market without disrupting policyholders. Firms must also secure independent internal-audit assurance over their exit preparations, and supervisors can now request the analysis at any time.

headline: AI-driven pay-per-mile insurer Mile Auto buys 62-year-old Georgia agency
summary: Mile Auto, an AI-powered managing general agent known for pay-per-mile auto coverage, completed its acquisition of The Insurance House, a longstanding Southeast agency, effective July 1. The combined operation now serves more than 55,000 policyholders through roughly 1,600 independent agencies across ten states.

headline: Gallagher's wholesale unit RPS scoops up Kansas-based MGA Med James
summary: Arthur J. Gallagher's Risk Placement Services arm acquired Med James, an Overland Park, Kansas managing general agency and wholesale broker with offices across five states, extending RPS's regional wholesale footprint. The deal follows RPS's other recent wholesale purchases, including Wilson M. Beck Insurance Services in Vancouver just days earlier.

headline: Arrow Global expands into specialty lines with Fusion Specialty MGA purchase
summary: Arrow Global Group announced it is acquiring Fusion Specialty Group, a specialist managing general agent, as part of a broader push by credit and asset manager Arrow into specialty insurance distribution. The deal adds underwriting and distribution capability to Arrow's existing financial services platform.

headline: Willis reshuffles Asia leadership with new Southeast Asia and regional commercial chiefs
summary: Willis (WTW) named Oliver Pryce as Head of Corporate Risk & Broking for Southeast Asia and Rupert Roberts as Chief Commercial Officer for Asia, both moves aimed at sharpening the broker's regional growth strategy. The appointments are part of a wider set of senior moves across the brokerage as competition for Asian corporate risk business intensifies.

headline: Broker Investment Group adds group COO to oversee retail and MGA integration
summary: The Broker Investment Group brought on Stuart Grieb as group chief operating officer effective July 13, giving him responsibility for operational execution across both its retail broking and MGA businesses. A second hire, Rosie Guru, joins the following week as group integration director, bringing transformation experience from RSA and NFP to support the group's consolidation strategy.

headline: India's fintech funding more than doubles quarter-on-quarter on jump in mega-deals
summary: Fintech investment in India climbed roughly 2.3 times sequentially in the second quarter of 2026, driven largely by a rise in deals exceeding $100 million, according to newly published funding data.

headline: SIAA-backed Sequel Insurance Agencies buys long-running Texas brokerage Watkins
summary: Sequel Insurance Agencies has acquired 76-year-old Watkins Insurance Group, adding five Austin-area and Central Texas offices and continuing a string of bolt-on acquisitions that push Sequel's network past $550 million in represented premium.

headline: BrokerTech Ventures sets September Chicago summit pairing carriers, brokers and AI vendors
summary: BrokerTech Ventures unveiled plans for its second BrokerTech Connect conference in Chicago this September, where technology sponsors including Vertafore and Fulcrum will showcase AI-powered tools for agency automation alongside the group's newly announced startup accelerator cohort.

headline: Tech-enabled MGA Bamboo rolls out budget homeowners product for harder-to-place homes
summary: Bamboo Insurance launched an Essential homeowners program aimed at price-sensitive buyers, designed to accept a broader range of properties, including older homes and those with prior claims, than many standard admitted-market policies allow.

headline: Cigna's Express Scripts sues Tennessee to block law forcing PBMs to divest pharmacies
summary: Express Scripts and the PCMA trade group filed a federal lawsuit challenging Tennessee's FAIR Rx Act, which would bar pharmacy benefit managers from owning pharmacies, arguing the law is unconstitutional and would shutter a major Memphis specialty pharmacy. CVS Caremark had already filed a similar challenge weeks earlier.

headline: Cigna completes CEO handoff as Evanko takes the reins from longtime chief Cordani
summary: The Cigna Group's leadership transition became effective, with President and COO Brian Evanko formally stepping into the CEO role while David Cordani, who led the company for nearly 17 years, moved into the executive chairman position after a multi-year succession plan.

headline: Managed-care stocks surge as Wall Street cheers cooler medical cost trends
summary: Shares of Humana, UnitedHealth and Cigna jumped after a wave of bullish analyst notes pointed to softening medical utilization and cost trends across the managed-care sector, with some analysts also flagging potential efficiency gains from AI adoption as a further tailwind.

headline: CMS stands up a dedicated office to police AI and digital health tools across Medicare
summary: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services created a new Office of Health Technology Products to coordinate oversight of artificial intelligence, interoperability and other emerging digital health technologies across its programs, signaling a bigger federal push to shape how AI is adopted in care delivery and program integrity.

headline: Principal Financial buys dental-benefits insurtech Beam in a sign M&A appetite is back
summary: Principal Financial Group agreed to acquire Beam Benefits, a technology-driven dental and vision insurance provider, in a deal that industry watchers say shows the employer health-benefits M&A market remains active despite a broader slowdown in insurance dealmaking.

headline: Highmark-owned Allegheny Health Network finalizes takeover of two Pennsylvania hospitals
summary: Allegheny Health Network completed its acquisition of Heritage Valley Health System's two acute-care hospitals in southwestern Pennsylvania, expanding the Highmark Health-owned network to 16 full-service inpatient facilities as the newly acquired sites are rebranded under the AHN name.

headline: Hospital dealmaking hits its busiest second quarter in years despite reimbursement uncertainty
summary: Hospitals and health systems recorded 18 M&A transactions in the second quarter of 2026, among the highest quarterly totals since 2018 and including three mega-mergers, according to a new Kaufman Hall report, suggesting consolidation momentum is holding up even as providers navigate reimbursement and policy uncertainty.

headline: MemorialCare completes long-planned leadership succession after 24-year CEO tenure
summary: California health system MemorialCare moved longtime CEO Barry Arbuckle into a new executive chairman role and elevated President David Kim to chief executive, capping a multi-year succession process the outgoing leader initiated with the board years in advance.

headline: Singapore and China deepen ties on medical AI as regional health-tech forum convenes
summary: Chinese and Singaporean health professionals gathered around the theme of designing an AI-driven healthcare future, part of a broader push across the Asia-Pacific region to close gaps in hospital adoption of AI-based diagnosis and remote-monitoring tools even as strategic investment in digital health infrastructure accelerates.

headline: Pediatric primary-care platform Pediatrica lands $28 million to expand across the Sun Belt
summary: Miami-based Pediatrica Health Group, which operates pediatric primary-care practices across Florida and Texas, closed a $28 million Series B led by Valspring Capital that it plans to use for organic growth, acquisitions and investment in value-based care capabilities.

headline: US annuity sales cross $100 billion for a tenth straight quarter
summary: LIMRA reported total US annuity sales of roughly $107 billion in the first quarter of 2026, extending an unprecedented streak of quarterly sales above the $100 billion mark and reinforcing forecasts that full-year 2026 volume will stay above $450 billion.

headline: Corebridge and Equitable combine in $22 billion deal to build a $1.5 trillion retirement giant
summary: Corebridge Financial and Equitable Holdings agreed to an all-stock merger that would create the largest annuity seller in the country by volume, serving more than 12 million customers with a combined $1.5 trillion in assets once the deal closes by year-end 2026.

headline: India forces life insurers onto new accounting standard, upending reported earnings
summary: IRDAI's board approved changes requiring life insurers to switch to Ind AS-based financial statements starting April 2026, a shift expected to significantly alter how carriers recognize and disclose profits and reserves.

headline: Asset-intensive reinsurance keeps expanding across Asia-Pacific life insurance
summary: Insurers in the region are increasingly using asset-intensive reinsurance and sidecar structures to manage capital under new solvency regimes taking effect in 2026, a trend that is now drawing closer regulatory scrutiny over concentration risk.

headline: UK clears the way for savers to be moved into collective pension schemes without asking first
summary: New regulations taking effect July 31, 2026 let UK defined-contribution pension benefits be transferred into authorised collective defined contribution (CDC) schemes without individual member consent, alongside rules enabling new multi-employer CDC arrangements.

headline: Squeezed on fees, retirement recordkeepers lean harder on AI and pooled plans for growth
summary: A 2026 industry survey found pooled employer plan adoption jumped nearly 45% year over year, with recordkeepers turning to artificial intelligence to cut costs even as some expect it to shrink their own headcount within a few years.

headline: Big asset managers post solid June AUM gains as markets climb
summary: Invesco disclosed preliminary assets under management of about $2.47 trillion at the end of June 2026, up nearly 1% month over month, as peers including AllianceBernstein and Artisan Partners also reported higher managed assets heading into second-quarter earnings.

headline: MetLife signals softer alternative-investment returns for the second quarter
summary: MetLife issued a preliminary estimate putting second-quarter 2026 variable investment income - largely returns from private equity and real estate funds - well below its full-year guidance pace, a cautious signal for insurers' alternative asset portfolios.

headline: AI-focused advisor startups drive an 83% jump in US wealthtech funding
summary: US wealthtech investment nearly doubled year over year in the first quarter of 2026, headlined by Jump, an AI platform for financial advisors, closing one of the period's largest rounds at $80 million.

headline: Independent advisory firm Modera brings in new investment and operations chiefs
summary: Modera Wealth Management named a new chief investment officer and chief operating officer, both wealth management veterans, as the RIA looks to expand its investment offerings and modernize its technology platform.

headline: AI compliance startup Norm AI rockets to unicorn status with insurer-backed $120M round
summary: Norm AI, an agentic legal and regulatory compliance platform, closed a $120 million Series C led by Khosla Ventures at a $1.2 billion valuation, with insurance and financial heavyweights New York Life, TIAA and Vanguard among the backers helping automate compliance reviews for regulated industries.

headline: Corgi rolls out liability coverage for businesses deploying their own AI systems
summary: Insurtech-fintech Corgi launched a new insurance product aimed at protecting companies from financial and legal fallout tied to the AI systems they build or deploy, targeting a fast-growing category of emerging tech risk.

headline: US health insurers push through steepest ACA marketplace premium hikes in years
summary: Insurers filed for roughly 21.7% average benchmark premium increases on 2026 ACA marketplace plans, the largest jump since 2018, driven by rising drug and medical costs including GLP-1 spending.

headline: Analysts warn under-governed AI models could become insurers' next compliance headache
summary: A trade analysis cautioned that insurers scaling AI across underwriting, claims and customer service without strong data governance risk inconsistent decisions and regulatory scrutiny as oversight of AI tightens worldwide.

headline: Agency management software leader Applied Systems taps insider Graham Blackwell as next CEO
summary: Applied Systems named longtime president Graham Blackwell as its incoming chief executive, succeeding Taylor Rhodes later in 2026, continuing a planned leadership transition at the insurance agency software provider.

headline: AI-native agency roll-up Equal Parts snaps up Texas independent agency D3
summary: Equal Parts, which buys independent insurance agencies and migrates them onto its AI operating platform Ultron, acquired Amarillo-based D3 Insurance, extending its roll-up strategy to a fourth state as it pursues $1 billion in premium within two years.

headline: Malaysian insurtech PolicyStreet tops up Series C to $26 million with impact investor BlueOrchard
summary: Southeast Asian insurtech PolicyStreet added $5 million more to its Series C round, bringing the total to $26 million, with new backing from impact investor BlueOrchard to fund regional expansion into mobility, travel and gig-economy insurance.

headline: Employee-benefits insurtech Plum raises ₹193 crore after turning profitable
summary: Indian B2B health-benefits platform Plum raised about $20.6 million in a Series B led by Peak XV Partners, nearly doubling its valuation, to invest in AI-driven claims operations and deepen HR and payroll integrations.

headline: MSIG Asia recruits QBE veteran Ronak Shah to lead its regional business
summary: Singapore-based insurer MSIG Asia named Ronak Shah, formerly CEO of QBE's Wholesale Markets Asia, as its new Regional CEO effective October 2026, giving him oversight of operations spanning Southeast Asia, Hong Kong, India, Oceania and Greater China.

headline: Brussels issues draft guidance on which insurance AI systems count as high-risk
summary: The European Commission released draft, non-binding guidelines clarifying when AI systems used in insurance underwriting and pricing fall under the EU AI Act's high-risk regime, ahead of an August 2026 compliance deadline for such systems.

headline: UnitedHealth pours $1.5 billion into AI to chase $1 billion in savings
summary: UnitedHealthcare's CEO said the insurer expects nearly $1 billion in AI-enabled operating cost reductions in 2026, backed by a $1.5 billion technology investment aimed at automating claims processing and member service through Optum.

headline: UnitedHealth, Centene and Elevance post recovering quarterly results
summary: All three major payers beat earnings expectations in their latest quarter, with analysts pointing to improved medical-cost management and stabilizing Medicaid and ACA margins as evidence of a broader insurer rebound after a rough 2025.

headline: Cigna hands CEO reins to longtime insider Brian Evanko
summary: After a multi-year succession process, Cigna's president and COO Brian Evanko took over as chief executive on July 1, 2026, with predecessor David Cordani moving into the executive chair role.

headline: Bupa reshuffles top leadership across its UK, India and European units
summary: Bupa named Chris Carroll to lead its Global, India and UK business while his predecessor Carlos Jaureguizar moves to head Bupa's Europe and Latin America division, part of a broader senior leadership shake-up effective January 2026.

headline: Australia approves near-4.5% private health insurance premium hike
summary: Australia's government signed off on an average 4.41% increase to private health insurance premiums from April 2026, citing rising hospital and medical service costs, while continuing to fund a multi-billion-dollar policyholder rebate.
source_name: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing

headline: Select Medical goes private in $3.9 billion insider-led buyout
